correctness.rationale: In the Type-II (1^2,2,3^2) case the nontrivial one-dimensional module fixes a three-dimensional simple, so the relevant grouplike stabilizer has order 2. Natale--Plavnik's Nichols--Zoeller consequence requires that stabilizer order to divide 3^2=9. Duality removes any left-versus-right tensor convention ambiguity. Thus Type II is impossible, and Martin Duro's remaining cases imply the dimension-at-most-31 conclusion.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2024 paper and its current arXiv version retain Type II as the sole exception, while targeted searches did not locate a later correction or equivalent observation. The general stabilizer-divisibility theorem is old; the claimed contribution is specifically the correction/application eliminating the exception.

value.rationale: The observation removes the unique exception from a published low-dimensional Knutson classification and yields an unconditional theorem for all semisimple Hopf algebras of dimension at most 31 under the stated base-field hypotheses.
